title: Disney Names Former Character.AI CEO Karandeep Anand Its First CTO
excerpt: The Indian-origin executive will take charge of Disney's companywide technology strategy on October 2 as artificial intelligence reshapes the media business.
body:
• Walt Disney has named Karandeep Anand, most recently CEO of generative-AI startup Character.AI, as its first chief technology officer — a newly created companywide role.
  • Anand will join Disney on October 2 as senior executive vice president and CTO, reporting directly to CEO Josh D'Amaro, overseeing enterprise technology, data and AI platforms, and engineering across all business segments.
  • The appointment carries an unusual twist: Disney sent Character.AI a cease-and-desist letter in September 2025 over its unauthorised use of Disney characters.
  • The Indian-origin executive spent 15 years at Microsoft helping build Azure, held senior roles at Meta, and served as president and chief product officer at fintech company Brex.

LOS ANGELES — Walt Disney on Friday named Karandeep Anand, the former chief executive of generative-AI startup Character.AI, as its first chief technology officer, a newly created companywide role that underscores how urgently Hollywood is racing to put artificial intelligence at the centre of its business.

Anand will join Disney effective October 2 as senior executive vice president and CTO, reporting directly to chief executive Josh D'Amaro, the theme parks veteran who took the reins from Bob Iger in March. He will oversee enterprise technology, infrastructure, data management and AI platforms, as well as product and engineering across Disney's businesses. A number of Character.AI's technical staff are expected to follow him to Disney, according to Reuters.

From cease-and-desist to the C-suite

The appointment carries a striking irony. In September last year, Disney sent Character.AI a cease-and-desist letter over the startup's unauthorised use of Disney characters on its platform. Character.AI removed the characters following the move.

Character.AI, a generative AI chatbot service that lets users interact with artificially created characters, has also been under legal scrutiny over chatbot safety. In May, it faced a lawsuit over chatbot impersonation of doctors, and in January it settled a wrongful-death suit tied to a teenager's suicide. Google also settled lawsuits brought by families who accused the technology of harming minors, including allegations linked to the suicide of a Florida teenager. Neither Character.AI nor Google disclosed the terms of the settlement or admitted liability.

Who is Karandeep Anand

The world of technology, including AI, is not new to Anand. Before Character.AI, he served as president and chief product officer at fintech company Brex. He also held senior roles at Meta's Facebook, most recently as vice president for ads and business products. Earlier in his career, he spent 15 years at Microsoft, where he helped build the Azure cloud platform, leaving as a director of product management.

Anand studied computer science at the International Institute of Information Technology in Hyderabad and later received marketing training from Northwestern University's Kellogg School of Management, according to his LinkedIn profile. He held the Character.AI CEO role for nearly two years before the Disney move.

Why Disney created the role now

Disney framed the appointment as a bet that technology — and AI in particular — must sit at the heart of its creative business as industry consolidation and generative AI disrupt the media landscape.

"Karandeep brings a rare mix of experience across infrastructure, consumer technology and AI, and will be a vital addition to Disney's senior leadership team as we further our three priorities: great storytelling as our North Star, technology in service of creativity, and operating as One Disney."

— Josh D'Amaro, CEO, Disney

D'Amaro also called Anand "an expert builder and strategist, technical and product-minded, with sharp instincts for what fans actually want."

For his part, Anand pointed to Disney's storytelling as the draw. "I've admired Disney my entire life for how it blends unforgettable storytelling with the latest technology," he said, adding that he wants to help "connect fans worldwide with its beloved stories and characters in new and innovative ways."

The CTO announcement came alongside other leadership moves: Disney named insider Adam Smith chairman of its streaming business and created a new television franchise role for Joe Earley, sharpening its focus on direct-to-consumer platforms such as Disney+ and Hulu.

An Indian-origin technologist at Hollywood's helm

Anand's appointment adds another name to the growing ranks of Indian-origin executives leading global technology strategy — a lineage that includes Satya Nadella at Microsoft and Sundar Pichai at Alphabet. For the diaspora, it is one more signal that the path from Indian engineering schools to the top of the world's largest entertainment company runs through deep technical and product expertise.

What to watch

Anand takes charge on October 2. The early tests: how quickly he articulates Disney's AI platform strategy, how much of Character.AI's technical team migrates with him, and how Disney balances aggressive AI adoption with the creative guardrails that matter to it — the same company once forced to police its characters on his own startup's platform.
